title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages). G is a group of multiplicative type over S, the Cartier dual of a sheaf of abelian groups M (an étale, fppf or fpqc sheaf). Its co-Lie complex is ℓ^G ≅ M ⊗^L_Z O_S, given by (1.3); with a coefficient ring Λ it is (M ⊗^L_Z Λ) ⊗^L_Λ O_S. Section 2 reads off its two cohomology sheaves:
- H^0 = ω_G = M ⊗_Z O_S (invariant differentials).
- H^{-1} = n_G = Tor_1^Z(M, O_S).

In characteristic p this gives ω_G = M_p ⊗_{F_p} O_S with M_p = M/pM, and n_G ≅ _pM ⊗_{F_p} O_S. If pM = 0 (that is, G is killed by p, e.g. G = μ_p^d), then ω_G ≅ n_G ≅ M ⊗_{F_p} O_S. This explains the non-smoothness of μ_p-type groups: n_G ≠ 0.

A two-term complex in the derived category is determined by its cohomology sheaves together with its Postnikov (k-)invariant. Here that invariant is ξ ∈ Ext^2_{O_S}(ω_G, n_G). Grothendieck observes that ξ comes from the k-invariant ξ_Λ ∈ Ext^2_Λ(M⊗Λ, Tor_1(M,Λ)) of M ⊗^L_Z Λ.

Take Λ = Z/n and M a locally free Λ-module of finite type. Then M⊗Λ ≅ M and Tor_1(M,Λ) = _nM ≅ M, so ξ_Λ ∈ H^2(S, End(M)). Similarly ξ ∈ H^2(S, End(E)) with E = M ⊗_Λ O_S, and ξ is the image of ξ_Λ under H^2(S, End M) → H^2(S, End M ⊗ O_S).

Next page. Suppose M descends from a representation π → Aut(M_0) along a principal covering, giving a morphism of topoi S → B_π. Then ξ_Λ comes from ξ_0 ∈ H^2(π, End M_0). By functoriality one may pass to the universal case π = GL_d(Z/n).

Following Illusie, ξ_0 is the obstruction to lifting the representation to a free Z/n²-module (Z/p² for n = p). For π = GL_d(F_p) this is the class of the extension 0 → M_d(F_p) → GL_d(Z/p²) → GL_d(F_p) → 1.
- For d = 1 it vanishes (Teichmüller lift).
- For d ≥ 2 it is conjectured to be nonzero.

Finally, if S' is the universal cover, H^2(π, −) → H^2(S, −) is injective. Hence one gets nonzero ξ_Λ, i.e. a co-Lie complex of a multiplicative-type group that does not split as ω_G ⊕ n_G[1].

Purpose: understanding the structure (non-decomposability) of ℓ^G for non-smooth groups of multiplicative type. This is relevant to deformation and crystalline questions in the 'Cristaux' notes.
errors: On the next page the lifting obstruction is first stated for Z/p² while Λ = Z/n is general; for general n it should be Z/n² (or the appropriate square-zero thickening). Grothendieck himself then restricts to n = p.

The guess 'sans doute pas nulle si d ≥ 2' is false for some small (d, p). For example, GL_2(Z/4) → GL_2(F_2) splits (S_3 lifts to GL_2(Z)), and SL_2(F_3) lifts to SL_2(Z_3) via the binary tetrahedral group. Generic nonvanishing holds (e.g. p ≥ 5), but the exact exceptional list should be checked (unsure for GL_2(F_3)).
Injectivity of H^2(π,A) → H^2(S,A) uses H^1(S̃, A) = 0 on the (pro-)universal cover, which holds for finite locally constant A. This is fine here since End(M_0) is finite, but it is left implicit.

ideas.what: Cohomology sheaves of the co-Lie complex of a multiplicative-type group: ω_G = M⊗O_S, n_G = Tor_1(M,O_S)
ideas.modern_name: co-Lie complex ℓ^G / invariant differentials and n_G
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 7 / co-Lie complex), Illusie (Complexe cotangent, ch. VII)
ideas.where_published: Illusie, Complexe cotangent et déformations II (groupes de type multiplicatif); SGA 7 exposé VII for ℓ^G

ideas.what: k-invariant ξ ∈ Ext^2(ω_G, n_G) of ℓ^G, induced from the k-invariant of M ⊗^L Z/n in H^2(S, End M)
ideas.modern_name: Postnikov/k-invariant of a two-term complex; obstruction to lifting M flatly mod n²
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (as stated in the text); cf. Deligne–Illusie decomposition criteria
ideas.where_published: Illusie, Complexe cotangent (statement that M ⊗^L Z/p splits iff M lifts flatly to Z/p²)

ideas.what: Universal case: obstruction class in H^2(GL_d(F_p), M_d(F_p)) of the extension GL_d(Z/p²) → GL_d(F_p), pulled back via S → B_π
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sah (1970s cohomology of split extensions); Serre for SL_2

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly links the non-decomposability of the co-Lie complex of a p-torsion multiplicative group G over a char-p base to group cohomology of GL_d(F_p), namely the non-splitting of GL_d(Z/p²) → GL_d(F_p). The transport is via the classifying morphism S → B_{π_1}. This is a neat, if elementary, observation; it is essentially implicit in Illusie's framework.
missed.quote: ξ_Λ ∈ H^2(S, End(M)) ... ξ ∈ H^2(S, End(E)) (E = M⊗_Λ O_S) et ξ se déduit de ξ_Λ par l'hom. can.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives explicit examples of non-split ℓ^G for twisted μ_p^d, relevant to deformation theory of finite flat group schemes. It is likely known to specialists and not new.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine computation of the co-Lie complex for multiplicative-type groups and its k-invariant, attributed by Grothendieck himself to Illusie. The link to GL_d(Z/p²) is natural and known.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'l'entier[?] de (1.3)' is more likely 'l'on tire de (1.3)' (i.e. 'Notons que l'on tire de (1.3)').
'il en est de même[?]' reads as 'il en est ainsi' / 'il en est de même'; the sense is that M⊗Λ and Tor_1 are also locally free.
The Ext and H superscripts read in the image as 'Ext^r'/'H^r' are 2: Ext², H².
